title: Use alerts to catch problems before your users do

blocks.content:
Some numbers are worth watching, like the response time of a checkout page or free disk space on a database server. They drift all day, and that's fine until one climbs high enough to cause trouble. Nobody can watch a chart waiting for that moment, so an alert rule does it for you.

Every few minutes, it checks the value against a threshold you set. Write the rule once, and Grafana Cloud keeps watch from then on. Grafana Play runs a demo rule like this. Its value is made up, but the rule is real. When the value climbs above its threshold of 75, the rule fires.

This guide walks you through alerting on Grafana Play. You'll see where alert rules are defined, check which alerts are firing right now, and open the demo rule to read its three working parts. Those are the query it runs, the threshold it checks, and the notifications it sends.
First, go where alert rules are defined.

Open **Alert rules**.

Every rule on Grafana Play is listed here. Each one watches a value and fires when it crosses a threshold. On your own Grafana, this page has a **New alert rule** button for writing a new one; Grafana Play hides it from visitors, so here you can look but not touch.
Rules are written once, on that page. From then on, Grafana runs them around the clock.
Next, see alerts that are firing right now.

Open **Alert activity**.

This is where you look when you want to know what's wrong right now.

Notice the **Firing** filter is already on.

Everything listed here has crossed its threshold. The count rises and falls as rules fire and recover.
blocks.tooltip: A live count of firing alerts. It climbs when rules fire and drops when the values recover.

blocks.content:
Scan the list.

Each row is one alert firing right now, grouped in folders. **Demo: Alerting** is Grafana Play's demo set, and the rule you're about to meet lives there.
blocks.tooltip: Grafana is watching these rules, and each one has already crossed its threshold.

blocks.content: You saw alerts in action. Firing means a rule's threshold was crossed, and **Alert activity** is where you look when something's wrong.
Next, meet the rule that does the watching.

Open **Random Single Serie**, one of the demo rules from the folder you just saw.

This rule watches a value that drifts on its own and fires when it climbs too high.

Look at the query the rule runs every few minutes.

The chart shows its result over time. This is the value the rule is watching.
blocks.tooltip: Grafana runs this query on the rule's schedule, whether or not anyone is looking.

blocks.content:
Read the **alert condition**.

This is the threshold the query result is compared against. When the result climbs above it, the rule fires.
blocks.tooltip: The rule fires when the query result crosses this threshold.

blocks.content:
Open the **Notifications** tab.

Firing isn't the end of the story. The rule sends a message to a person or channel, so someone can act, and this tab keeps the record of every message it has sent.
blocks.tooltip: When the rule fires, Grafana notifies someone, and the history of those notifications lives here.

blocks.content: You write a rule once, and Grafana Cloud takes it from there. It runs the query, checks the threshold, and sends the notification. When you're ready to write a rule of your own, the Grafana Alerting 101 guide walks you through it.
